stories.title: SpiceJet faces DGCA notice over operational failures
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation has issued a show-cause notice to SpiceJet following a decline in on-time performance and frequent flight cancellations. The regulator has given the airline seven days to explain the operational lapses and the inadequate support provided to affected passengers.

stories.title: SpiceJet under scrutiny for selling cancelled flights
stories.summary: SpiceJet faces a seven-day show-cause notice from the DGCA regarding operational lapses and grounded aircraft. Passengers allege the airline continues to sell tickets for flights that have been cancelled, while refunds for those affected remain delayed. The airline has yet to resolve the mounting disruptions.

stories.title: SpiceJet passengers confront staff amid flight cancellations
stories.summary: Chaos erupted at Delhi airport after a SpiceJet flight to Mumbai was cancelled following hours of delay. The airline has scrapped most of its schedule in recent days amid deepening financial trouble, leaving passengers to confront staff and demand answers regarding their missing refunds.

stories.title: Navi Mumbai airport records highest daily traffic
stories.summary: Navi Mumbai International Airport handled more than 200 flight movements on Thursday, marking its highest daily figure to date. The airport is designed to handle 90 million passengers annually, with several major carriers preparing to shift international services to the facility during terminal redevelopment.

stories.title: Delhi airport chaos: SpiceJet flights cancelled after hours of delay, passengers stranded, DGCA issues notice to airline
SpiceJet seeks funds to combat operational crisis
stories.summary: SpiceJet is attempting to raise 5,500 crore rupees to stabilize its finances as it battles a shrinking fleet and declining market share. The airline faces mounting regulatory scrutiny and passenger complaints, with the DGCA flagging multiple compliance lapses as the carrier struggles to maintain operations.

stories.title: SpiceJet warned of potential shutdown by regulator
stories.summary: The DGCA has given SpiceJet seven days to improve its performance or face a potential flight ban. The airline is currently operating roughly 20 flights a day, with three in four domestic services delayed or cancelled. The carrier has also suspended all international flights.

stories.title: SpiceJet domestic market share drops to 0.6 percent
stories.summary: The DGCA has issued a show-cause notice to SpiceJet following widespread cancellations and delays. The airline's domestic market share fell to 0.6 percent in October, with on-time performance reaching 25 percent on November 19. The board has approved a proposal to raise 5,500 crore rupees.

stories.title: Notice to SpiceJet over lapses: DGCA flags flight delays, cancellations and grounded fleet - Telegraph India
Korean Air receives 10th consecutive five-star rating
stories.summary: The Airline Passenger Experience Association has named Korean Air a 2027 Five-Star Global Airline for the 10th consecutive year. The rating is based on passenger feedback, and the carrier also received two additional awards for seat comfort and service at the recent APEX FTE EXPO.

stories.title: Emirates opens temporary first class lounge in Dubai
stories.summary: Emirates has unveiled a new First Class Lounge at Dubai International Airport, part of a 400 million dirham transformation of its flagship spaces. The lounge will serve First Class customers for one year before being converted into a next-generation Business Class facility.

stories.title: Delta flight delayed after cat escapes kennel
stories.summary: A Delta Air Lines flight to Tampa was delayed by 15 minutes at Boston Logan International Airport after a passenger's cat escaped its kennel and roamed the cabin. The crew held the aircraft on the taxiway until the animal was secured.

stories.title: Avelo Airlines cuts 31 routes for winter season
stories.summary: Avelo Airlines has removed 31 routes from its winter 2026/27 schedule compared to the previous year. The cuts include 25 domestic and six international services, with a third of the domestic reductions concentrated at a single airport. The airline says it remains in flux.

stories.title: Delta cancels short-haul widebody route
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines has removed its planned Airbus A350-900 service between Las Vegas and Los Angeles from its latest schedule. The airline had intended to use the widebody aircraft for the roughly one-hour flight, one of over 17,000 domestic widebody flights scheduled through next October.

stories.title: United Airlines maintains unique overseas hub in Guam
stories.summary: United Airlines remains the only US carrier with an overseas hub, operating out of Guam. The airline currently runs up to 12 daily flights to 15 destinations across five countries from the territory, continuing a legacy operation that dates back nearly 60 years.

stories.title: Airports struggle with baggage backlog after ground stop
stories.summary: Hundreds of unclaimed bags remained at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport following last week's nationwide FAA ground stop. Airport officials noted that excess baggage is a common result of widespread flight disruptions, as airlines work to reunite passengers with their stranded property.

stories.title: Travel advisor suggests packing tips to avoid luggage loss
stories.summary: Travel advisor Whytney Rawls recommends that passengers separated from their luggage during flight disruptions file reports directly with their airlines and monitor status updates via mobile apps. She also suggests vacuum-sealing clothes to maximize carry-on space and avoid checking bags entirely.

stories.title: Embraer and Envoy Air extend heavy maintenance agreement
stories.summary: Embraer and Envoy Air have extended their heavy maintenance agreement for E-Jet aircraft in the United States. Supplemental services will continue at Embraer facilities in Macon, Georgia, and Fort Worth, Texas. Envoy, a wholly-owned subsidiary of American Airlines, currently operates 189 of the jets.

stories.title: Amentum receives $38.3 million in aviation maintenance awards
stories.summary: Amentum Services received $38.3 million in Army aviation maintenance modifications and two major contract vehicle positions. The awards include $18.4 million for worldwide maintenance support and $19.9 million for additional services. The funding was obligated using fiscal 2027 aircraft procurement and operations budgets.

stories.title: Boeing weighs more layoffs as 737 MAX production lags
stories.summary: Boeing declined to tell its largest union if further layoffs will follow next month's planned cuts. The company is struggling to increase 737 MAX output to 47 jets per month, a rate it expected to reach this summer. It now targets early 2027 for that goal.

stories.title: Airlines prepare for the delayed Boeing 777-9
stories.summary: Boeing has roughly 620 orders for the 777-9, an aircraft that has yet to reach a single customer. The program is seven years behind its original 2020 service date. For an industry that plans fleets decades in advance, the start of this new era remains elusive.

stories.title: Boeing parks 30 finished 777X jets
stories.summary: More than 30 Boeing 777X aircraft are parked in Washington State because their current configurations do not meet final delivery standards. Boeing and customers including Lufthansa and Emirates are in disagreement over the jets. The aircraft require additional modifications before they can be accepted for commercial service.

stories.title: Lufthansa receives A350-1000 before delayed 777-9
stories.summary: Lufthansa has begun receiving Airbus A350-1000 aircraft while waiting for its Boeing 777-9s. The airline ordered the 777-9 in 2013, ten years before its A350-1000 order. Boeing currently targets 2027 for the first 777-9 deliveries, seven years after the jet was originally scheduled to enter service.

stories.title: Trump claims credit for Philippine Airlines Boeing order
stories.summary: President Trump claimed he persuaded Philippine Airlines to order 20 Boeing 787s instead of Airbus jets. The airline finalized the Boeing deal this month, though it also recently firmed up an order for nine Airbus A350-1000s. The carrier remains a customer of both manufacturers.

stories.title: Boeing's parked 777-9 fleet awaits delivery
stories.summary: Boeing is targeting 2027 for first 777-9 deliveries after accumulating 4,800 flight hours in testing. Meanwhile, more than 30 completed or substantially completed airframes remain parked in Washington. The certification project continues as the company works through remaining regulatory approvals and required modifications for the stored jets.

stories.title: Air Canada confirms order for eight Airbus A350-1000s
stories.summary: Air Canada has confirmed a firm order for eight Airbus A350-1000 aircraft to support its long-haul network. The order, previously listed as undisclosed, will enable non-stop services to the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, and Australia. The airline is expanding its commitment to Airbus widebody aircraft.

stories.title: FBI and TSA warn of aviation security threats
stories.summary: The FBI, DHS, and TSA issued a report warning airlines of Al Qaeda affiliates praising September's attempted hijacking of a Flydubai flight. The notice encourages followers to carry out similar attacks against US and Israeli targets. It arrives just before the busiest travel week of the year.

stories.title: Lawmakers question FAA funding request
stories.summary: Lawmakers expressed skepticism over a $50 billion FAA funding request following a nationwide ground stop. The proposal aims to coordinate and upgrade 50-year-old equipment. Debate continues on whether additional government spending will resolve the communication failures that recently disrupted the national air traffic system.

stories.title: House panel urges FAA to reject Chinese aircraft
stories.summary: The U.S. House Select Committee on China recommended that the FAA reject certification for aircraft manufactured in China. The nonbinding report cited the lack of a final investigation into the 2022 China Eastern crash. The panel argued that U.S. certification would reward state-backed aerospace interests.

stories.title: DOT watchdog to audit FAA supplier oversight
stories.summary: The Department of Transportation’s Office of Inspector General will audit FAA oversight of aircraft manufacturers' quality controls for suppliers. Auditors plan to begin in December. The FAA recently changed how it assesses manufacturing risks and introduced a new system for tracking its oversight work.

stories.title: System failures hit banks and aviation
stories.summary: A series of technology outages between November 12 and November 17 disrupted Microsoft, Chase, and the FAA. The FAA ground stop delayed flights at Houston airports, while other failures affected United Airlines and Apple. Officials have reported no evidence that the major outages were connected.

stories.title: Travelers face fallout from FAA ground stop
stories.summary: A rare nationwide FAA ground stop delayed or canceled more than 12,000 flights last week. The incident was the second of its kind since 2001. Federal officials stated the disruption began at 3:30 p.m. Eastern time, leaving passengers stranded in airports and hotels across the country.

stories.title: FAA ground stop highlights aging infrastructure
stories.summary: A nationwide FAA ground stop canceled thousands of flights last week, leaving travelers stranded at airports like JFK. The incident prompted questions about the reliability of the air traffic control system. The president-elect of the American Society of Civil Engineers noted the system relies on antique network infrastructure.

stories.title: Federal report shows mixed airline performance
stories.summary: Federal data through September shows United Airlines mishandled the most checked bags, while Delta’s cancellation rate rose sharply. American Airlines reduced involuntary denied boardings. The figures cover domestic operations and highlight uneven year-over-year performance across baggage handling, punctuality, and cancellations for major carriers.

stories.title: FBI database reported breached after tech outages
stories.summary: The FBI is investigating a breach of the National Crime Information Center database. The intrusion was discovered following a series of technology disruptions that hit US banks and aviation. The database is a central system used by law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information.

stories.title: K-State Salina selected as an inaugural NOAA Cooperative Aviation Center
stories.summary: Kansas State University Salina is one of three universities selected for the new NOAA Cooperative Aviation Centers. The program aims to create a pipeline of qualified pilots for the NOAA Corps. Legislation signed in 2020 established the training program that evolved into this new partnership model.

stories.title: Aviation academy ordered to refund student after two-year delay
stories.summary: A Bengaluru consumer commission ordered an aviation academy to refund 10 lakh rupees plus interest after the school failed to start training courses despite collecting full fees. The academy must also pay 20,000 rupees for mental distress and legal costs. The training never took off.

stories.title: SkyWorthiness partners with US Aviation Academy for pilot training
stories.summary: Mumbai-based SkyWorthiness has partnered with the US Aviation Academy to offer Indian students a pathway to FAA pilot training in Texas. The platform provides theoretical preparation and documentation support but does not conduct flight training itself. It was founded earlier this year to assist student pilots.

stories.title: SkyWorthiness partners with US Aviation Academy for pilot training
stories.summary: Indian aviation mentorship platform SkyWorthiness has announced a partnership with the US Aviation Academy to provide Indian students a pathway to FAA pilot training in Texas. The arrangement combines pre-departure theory in India with practical flight training in Denton. The platform does not conduct the flight training itself.

stories.title: Wiley Post Airport breaks ground on new 13 million dollar control tower
stories.summary: Wiley Post Airport has begun construction on a new 13 million dollar air traffic control tower. Oklahoma City officials state the facility will improve safety and support regional growth. The executive director of the state's aerospace department noted that a tower is the hallmark of an airport.

stories.title: Global professional pilot workforce estimated at 441,000
stories.summary: CAE estimates 441,000 professional pilots worked worldwide in 2025, while Boeing reports 315,000 active commercial pilots for larger aircraft. No global pilot register exists, meaning workforce estimates depend entirely on definitions and scope. Forecasts of pilot shortages inherit these differences in how a pilot is counted.

stories.title: Virgin Atlantic targets RAF pilots for commercial recruitment
stories.summary: Virgin Atlantic has targeted Royal Air Force pilots for recruitment as the UK military faces a shortage of trained fighter jet pilots. Training a single F-35 pilot costs approximately 10 million dollars, with annual graduation numbers often in the single digits. The military lacks depth in its pilot pool.

stories.title: Airbus cruise crew reduction plan stalls under regulators
stories.summary: Regulators in the US and Europe maintain a two-pilot minimum for commercial flights, keeping Airbus plans to reduce cruise crews on hold. Long-haul flights currently carry up to four pilots to satisfy rest regulations. Crew costs remain tied to the current rules for flight duration.

stories.title: Polk State Aerospace Symposium connects students with industry leaders
stories.summary: Polk State College held its inaugural Aerospace Symposium to connect students with local airport leaders and industry professionals. The event focused on career paths and workplace challenges. It reflects the college president's initiative to prepare students for the daily work of navigating government organizations and changing technology.

research.title: Scientists create a remarkable new rechargeable battery using vitamin B12
research.summary: Scientists have found a surprising new use for vitamin B12, developing a rechargeable battery that uses the essential nutrient to help generate and store electricity. The prototype survived up to 250 charging cycles and could open the door to safer, cheaper, and more environmentally friendly alternatives to lithium-ion.
